profile.campus: Google Central Ohio (New Albany / Columbus-Lockbourne / Lancaster), OH
profile.address: Babbitt Road, New Albany, Plain Township, Franklin County, OH 43004 (3)
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's New Albany, Ohio data center campus, mapped on Babbitt Road in Plain Township, and carries the informational label NBY-2 in this registry's underlying mapping data, not independently confirmed against a Google-published building index this session; the county field in this registry's underlying data lists Licking County for this row, though the coordinate falls within the New Albany campus area near the Franklin/Licking county line. Google's own Ohio locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Ohio data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company broke ground in New Albany in 2019 and has since invested more than $20 billion in the state across New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus, generating $21.7 billion in Ohio economic activity in 2025 and contributing over $16 million in philanthropic giving since 2006.

New Albany has become the anchor of Ohio's central data center corridor since Google broke ground there in 2019, though Google's own public materials describe its New Albany footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) is the principal electric utility serving most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market, and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load electric tariff structures in response to rapidly growing data center demand in the corridor. New Albany's community authority has used tax-increment financing agreements, and Ohio's state-level data center sales and use tax abatement program, to help anchor the cluster's continued growth alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Google NBY-2 is part of a multi-county data center campus in the New Albany and Columbus area that Google has committed $1.7 billion to develop across Franklin, Licking, and Fairfield counties. Google does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for individual buildings within this campus, only aggregate state-level investment figures. This facility-level opacity is Google's stated disclosure policy and prevents direct measurement of this building's capacity.

Within Ohio's mapped data center infrastructure, which includes 76 facilities, only 8 operators have published power figures totaling 60.4 MW of disclosed capacity. NBY-2 does not appear among those 8 published specs, placing it outside Ohio's ranked set by disclosed megawatts. The New Albany corridor where NBY-2 sits has also attracted AWS and Meta as major hyperscale investors, indicating this region has become a preferred cluster for large operators, though individual facility capacities remain undisclosed.

Without published specifications, NBY-2's relevance to AI scaling cannot be measured against the binding grid constraints this site tracks. The investment scale and hyperscaler concentration suggest material significance to regional power demand and supply planning, but translating that into racks, accelerators, or grid load requires assumptions about typical utilization densities that would obscure rather than clarify the actual deployment.
